title: MemPlan: Memory-Conditioned PDDL Planning for Partially Observable Text Environments
abstract: arXiv:2610.30379v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: LLM agents are flexible in language interaction, but using them as long-horizon planners is costly and prone to hallucinated or invalid actions. This paper targets a different role for LLMs: constrained bridges between language and symbolic planning. We propose MemPlan, a memory-conditioned PDDL planning framework for partially observable interactive text environments. MemPlan keeps the PDDL domain fixed and reconstructs the PDDL problem at each step from parsed observations, candidate hypotheses, and interaction memory. Positive graph memory assigns relevance-based action costs to candidate hypotheses for missing objects, locations, or conditions, guiding the planner toward more plausible checks. Negative memory records execution-refuted assumptions and compiles them into exclusion constraints, preventing repeated attempts at candidates already contradicted by feedback. translated_title: MemPlan：面向部分可观测文本环境的记忆条件化PDDL规划
translated_abstract: LLM智能体在语言交互方面具有灵活性，但将它们用作长程规划器不仅成本高昂，而且容易产生幻觉或无效动作。本文为LLM提出了另一种角色定位：作为语言与符号规划之间受约束的桥梁。我们提出了MemPlan，一个面向部分可观测交互式文本环境的记忆条件化PDDL规划框架。MemPlan保持PDDL域固定不变，并在每一步根据解析的观测结果、候选假设和交互记忆重建PDDL问题。正向图记忆为缺失对象、位置或条件的候选假设分配基于相关性的动作成本，引导规划器进行更合理的检查验证。负向记忆记录被执行结果反驳的假设，并将其编译为排除约束，防止对已被反馈否定的候选项进行重复尝试。通过一个统一的模式条件化语言-符号接口进行训练……
tldr: MemPlan提出了一种记忆条件化的PDDL规划框架，利用正向图记忆为候选假设分配基于相关性的动作成本、利用负向记忆将已被反驳的假设编译为排除约束，使LLM作为语言与符号规划之间的受约束桥梁，在部分可观测文本环境中有效减少幻觉和无效动作。
en_tdlr: MemPlan is a memory-conditioned PDDL planning framework that assigns relevance-based action costs to candidate hypotheses via positive graph memory and compiles execution-refuted assumptions into exclusion constraints via negative memory, enabling LLMs to serve as constrained bridges between language and symbolic planning while reducing hallucinated and invalid actions in partially observable text environments.
